full_judgment:
The petitioner is a national of Bangladesh aged about sixty years. She along with her husband Mr. Ehsan Ali migrated from India and became domicile of Bangladesh in the year 1949 and settled at Lalmonirhat under the greater Rangpur District. The petitioner's husband Mr. Ehsan Ali was an Assistant. Sub-Inspector of Police since 1950 and retired from the government service in the year 1984 

 10. An affidavit-in-opposition has been' filed on behalf of respondent No. 1 stating, inter aliathat the petitioner left Lalmonirhat during the War of Liberation of Bangladesh and her whereabouts were not known and, as such, the property became vested and was given on rent by the Government. The respondent No. 1 has not denied that the disputed property is owned by the petitioner but has stated that the disputed land appears to have been recorded in the name of Ambika Charan. However, it appears to us from Annexure-B that the petitioner has purchased these properties from the said Ambika Charan as early as 1959 and has been paying rent in repect of the property. There is, therefore, only one question to be decided and that is, whether the property is an abandoned property under President's Order 16 of 1972. The petitioner has stated that she and her family have all along been living in Bangladesh and also during the war of liberation, and she never left Bangladesh. Her husband was an Assistant Sub- Inspector of Police in 1950 and retired from the service in the year 1984 and died on 1.3.85. We can take note of the fact that the situation at Lalmonirhat from 25.3.71 till end of December may not have been favourable for the non-locals and so the petitioner and her caretaker left the property at Lalmonirhat for safety. It appears from Annexure-A' to the petition that the petitioner as early as on 11.11.72 swore an affidavit before the SDO Nilphamari that she, her husband and their children were all along living at Lalmonirhat. That her house, landed property, etc. situated at Lalmonirhat were left by her out of fear and she and her children took shelter at Syedpur and have been living there since then. She has also affirmed that all her children have decided to live in Bangladesh, not to go to any other country, that she was a Bengali national, loyal and faithful to Bangladesh. We have seen that her name appears in the voters' list and the pass-book of Habib Bank Ltd. Syedpur Branch (which was re-named Agrani Bank) from 1971 to 1977 shows that she had been operating her bank account and living in Bangladesh. In the circumstances it cannot be said that the petitioner's whereabouts were not known and that her property was abandoned under President's Order 16 of 1972.
